beats.text: They were headed for a picnic in Michigan City. 844 of them never left the dock.
beats.label: JULY 24, 1915

beats.text: On July 24, 1915, Western Electric workers and their families boarded the steamer Eastland in Chicago.
beats.label: THE PICNIC

beats.text: About 2,500 people were aboard. Still tied up in the Chicago River, the ship rolled over onto its side.
beats.label: THE CHICAGO RIVER

beats.text: 844 people died. It's the deadliest shipwreck on the Great Lakes.
Today, beside the Old Lighthouse in Michigan City, an anchor chain stretches across the grounds. 844 links. One for each person who died.
beats.label: THE MEMORIAL
beats.credit: Michigan City Historical Society; historical marker

beats.text: And in Chicago, people say that from the river bridges, they still see faces in the water.
beats.label: WHAT PEOPLE SAY
beats.credit: Legend: CBS Chicago (2021); Ghost Research Society

beats.label: WE REMEMBER
beats.credit: Michigan City Historical Society; Associated Press
